newsitem.title: UK: Wickes cash call, restructure gets go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Wickes cash call, restructure gets go ahead.

text.p: Troubled home improvement retailer Wickes Plc on Monday said shareholders had approved plans for a rights issue and capital restructuring at an extraordinary meeting.

Last month the retailer, whose former chiefs are being investigated for fraud, proposed a major refinancing, including a 53 million pound rights issue, a capital reduction of 100 million and new banking facilities of 52 million.
Wickes ran into trouble after the discovery of accounting irregularities dating back five years left it with a deficit on its profit and loss account.

The refinancing aims to put the group on the road to recovery, but a bidder may well pounce in the meantime, according to retail analysts, who have put a price tag of around 200 million pounds on the company.
Wickes said the capital reorganisation would become effective on January 7, when its shares are due to resume trading after being suspended since June.
The group has said it expected to make a loss before tax in 1996 of 56 million pounds. --London Newsroom +44 71 324 7974
